Sundays at St. Brendan's

Two services, one welcome.

Whether you prefer the quiet of a spoken liturgy or the lift of choral music, there is a place for you on Sunday morning.

8:00 AM
Holy Eucharist · Rite I

A spoken, contemplative service in traditional Prayer Book language. About 35 minutes. Followed by coffee in the parish hall.

What to expect →

10:00 AM
Choral Eucharist · Rite II

Our principal service, with the parish choir, hymns, and a sermon. About 70 minutes. Children are warmly welcome.

What to expect →

10:00 AM
Children & Families

Sunday School for ages 3–12 begins at the start of the 10 AM service and joins the congregation in time for communion.

Meet the team →

Last Sunday · June 21, 2026 · Proper 7, Pentecost +4

The Man Among the Tombs

Luke 8:26–39 · Galatians 3:23–29 · Psalm 22:19–28

The Rev. Hannah Wycliffe sits with the Gerasene demoniac, the herd of pigs, and the question of what we do with the people our communities have decided are too much — and what Jesus does instead.

Ways to participate

Four doors, one community.

However you find your way in, you'll find people already at work. Pick a door — or knock on more than one.

Worship

Join us Sunday morning, midweek, or for evensong at the cove. The liturgy is the work of the whole people of God.

Our community

A small church with a long table.

We are about a hundred and forty souls — fishermen and retired teachers, a few young families, a college student or two home for the summer, and the people you'd expect to find in a small Maine town in midsummer. Some of us have been here since we were baptized in this font; others walked in for the first time last Sunday and stayed for coffee.

We try to do a few things well: pray honestly, sing on the notes we can reach, look out for our neighbors, and not pretend the world is simpler than it is. The Episcopal Church gives us a deep tradition to draw on, and the freedom to bring our whole selves to it.

If you're new to all of this, that's wonderful. We were too, once.
